model_comparison.resume_claim_defense: Claim 1 ('lowered RUL error by 15% ... with engineered temporal features') maps to mlp_temporal_vs_raw_mlp = 15.9%: adding lag/rolling/EMA temporal features to the same MLP lowered test MAE from 10.81 to 9.09.
model_comparison.limitations: C-MAPSS is simulated turbofan data; numbers are FD001 test-split, single seed, local CPU run. Not a live-fleet result.

deployed_api.reason: not deployed — no AWS endpoint measured

cpu_vs_gpu.conclusion: GPU was UNAVAILABLE on this host, so only CPU was measured. The single-request CPU p99 is well under the 300 ms SLO (batch_1 p99 = 0.0662 ms), so the low-latency path is served on CPU. The 'GPU acceleration' claim remains a code-supported capability that is UNVERIFIED on hardware here — it must be benchmarked on a CUDA host to assert a throughput benefit.

scale_load_test.saturation: throughput plateaus ~300 rps at 25->50 users while p99 rises 160->270 ms; single uvicorn worker is CPU-bound on the sync inference path
scale_load_test.reason: single uvicorn worker on loopback; NOT an AWS/multi-node result

retraining.promotion: guarded — challenger must beat incumbent MAE by 5%; weaker rejected

monitoring.status: implemented + config/unit tested; no live-traffic render

claim_2_retrain_below_80.evidence: retrain_config 0.80 threshold + retrain_guard states + tests; Prometheus model_rolling_accuracy; guarded promotion
claim_2_retrain_below_80.caveat: controlled feedback, not live production labels

claim_3_under_300ms_gpu_redis_async.defensible_parts: under-300ms local (compute p99≈0.65ms, API p99≈2.1ms); Redis cache measured (hit p99≈0.14ms, real server); load-tested to ~300 rps with p99<300ms; async FastAPI
claim_3_under_300ms_gpu_redis_async.unverified_parts: GPU benefit (no CUDA), deployed AWS-endpoint latency (not deployed), multi-worker/multi-node scale
